# Microsoft Azure Database for PostgreSQL management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Database for PostgreSQL is a relational database service in the Microsoft cloud based on the PostgreSQL open source relational database.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Database for PostgreSQL resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Database for PostgreSQL management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.PostgreSql
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

decisions.reason: The three CodeGenMember attributes map TLS10, TLS11 and TLS12 to the named public members in a source file outside Generated; the member-name override and citations are directly supported.
Six CodeGenMember attributes and corresponding public members explicitly change version-member names in a source file outside Generated.

The cited guard is real, but this same method and file also supply an explicit property-by-property JSON reader. Treat that one method as one serialization behavior, including the empty masterServerId guard, rather than overlooking the broader reader or reporting a duplicate omission.

finding.subtype: Explicit server JSON reader with empty identifier handling
finding.explanation: DeserializePostgreSqlServerData reads JSON properties into model fields, including nested properties; it skips an empty masterServerId rather than constructing a ResourceIdentifier, and returns a PostgreSqlServerData from the parsed values.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The complete deserializer is supplied in src/Custom outside Generated, with the empty-string branch explicitly delimited by customized-code comments; the file's location, not the comments alone, establishes handwritten provenance.

decisions.reason: CodeGenType explicitly associates ArmPostgreSqlModelFactory with ArmPostgreSqlFlexibleServersModelFactory in the supplied src/Custom file.

The three specified CodeGenSuppress signatures appear on the factory at lines 20, 21 and 23; unlike the nearby backup and migration suppressions, no matching replacement body occurs in the captured lines. This supports suppression, not a claim about code beyond the excerpt.
The factory suppresses the string-input signature and provides an overload taking backup settings, converting the optional SAS URI sequence to store details before constructing the output model.

The cited factory builds a patch from public inputs and invokes a private converter that maps nested secret parameters to patch-model fields. Both behaviors are parts of the same factory's output-model adaptation in src/Custom.

The method is explicitly marked Obsolete and editor-hidden, points callers to the newer Entra type, and still constructs the former Active Directory type. This is evidence for a compatibility shim rather than speculation about its implementation history.
The captured factory parses a status string, translates nullable bools into enabled/disabled states, initializes lists and assigns additional internal collections on its constructed model.

The editor-hidden eight-argument SKU factory forwards to a longer signature with two defaults; this directly supports a retained shorter callable overload. Earlier release usage cannot be established from the excerpt.
The editor-hidden four-argument version factory forwards to a longer signature with one default; the callable shorter overload is directly visible, although prior release usage is not.

The editor-hidden factory overload forwards to a longer signature while inserting a default for supported features. The shorter signature is visible; no claim about the precise historical release is needed.
The cited method parses a status string, defaults and copies both input sequences, constructs an edition capability and sets its internal server-version collection in src/Custom.
The editor-hidden factory constructs a fast-provisioning capability from three caller inputs and supplies defaults for the other constructor arguments, as claimed.

limitations: Coverage is partial: 4 of 758 eligible files were captured. The model factory is limited to lines 1–275; the hyperscale factory documentation at its end has no supplied signature or body and is not reported.
Skipped file paths are coverage metadata, not evidence of their contents; no findings are inferred from them.

Generated counterpart signatures and earlier releases were not supplied. Short forwarding signatures are reported as compatibility-shaped overloads, without asserting a measured release history or current generator capability.

Only four of 758 eligible source files were captured, and the model factory excerpt ends at line 275 just before an additional declaration; no conclusions about omitted files or the rest of that factory are warranted.

Generated counterparts and release history are not supplied. Attribute semantics and factory overloads are visible, but precise previous-release API usage and generator behavior cannot be independently checked from these excerpts.
The explicit server JSON reader and its empty-identifier branch share one method, file, symbols and stable key; the revised finding covers them without a duplicate omission.
